# Teaching the Machine {.unnumbered}

Part I gave the warehouse mobile manipulator a measured body, a chunked proposer slot, and a permission path that bounds every motion segment by a chunk lease. Teaching that proposer a contact skill, such as unlatching a spring-latched cage door, exposes a difficulty that offline machine learning benchmarks never face. In a static benchmark, a classifier reads held-out examples drawn from a fixed distribution ($\ModelInput \sim \StaticDataDistribution$) whose next stored example never changes when the model predicts. On a physical machine, every action the permission path admits moves the arm, alters the contact state, and shapes the observations that follow. That closed-loop dependency is the second bedrock law of @sec-boundary-bedrock-laws, a systems design principle that turns covariate shift into an evidentiary discipline across data collection, training, and evaluation.

::: {#pri-vol4-endogenous-drift .callout-principle title="Endogenous data"}

**Invariant**: A physical agent's actions choose its next observations ($\PhysicalWorldState_{t+1} \sim \EnvironmentTransitionDistribution(\PhysicalWorldState \mid \PhysicalWorldState_{t}, \CognitivePolicyAction_{t})$), so the states a deployed policy visits need not be the states it was trained or tested on. For behavioral cloning, the worst-case cost of that drift can grow with the square of the horizon [@ross2011reduction], as @eq-data-quadratic-drift states.

**Implication**: A learned proposer's competence is a claim about a declared region of states, established in closed loop with the permission path in place. Visiting a state during collection, recording an attributable training target for it, and testing competence there in closed loop are three separate steps. Missing states call for more collection, and a finite set of trials bounds the resulting claim rather than proving it outright.

:::

Part II traces the cage-door policy across the machine Part I built. During collection the permission path can clamp or refuse an operator's command, and the body can deliver motion that differs from the admitted one. A demonstration must therefore show what was requested, what the permission path allowed, and what the body actually did. Part I's limit and handoff records become preconditions on the data. Training then turns the supported behavior into candidate policies, one cloned from the demonstrations and one distilled from a simulator teacher, each of which improves its training score while hiding a dependency the hardware can expose. Closed-loop trials test a candidate under declared conditions, showing how data collection, training, and evaluation fit together. When a displaced latch plate breaks the nominal policy, a recovery campaign collects attributable corrections, trains an updated candidate, and tests both nominal regression and the wider latch range (using stipulated trial counts rather than measurements from a physical robot).

* **Physical Data (@sec-data):** Decides which conditions the demonstrations support and what they cost to collect, and produces the provenance record of the demonstrations, which lists the conditions the data does not cover as known absences.
* **Policy Training (@sec-training):** Decides which training regime fits the available experience and which dependency each regime leaves hidden, and produces the policy manifest, whose declared operating domain cannot exceed the conditions the provenance record supports.
* **Closed-Loop Evaluation (@sec-evaluation):** Decides what a finite set of closed-loop trials supports about the proposer, and produces the evaluation record for a target operational design domain (ODD) inside the manifest's declared one, separating proposer autonomy, whole-machine task completion, and protective outcomes.

Part II hands forward an evaluation record: a claim about the learned proposer confined to a target ODD, the finite-sample bound that supports it, a catalog of the conditions it does not cover, and the runtime monitors the rest of the machine must supply. With it, the first of the record chain's two strands, plant limits and evaluated competence, is complete. That record identifies the candidate from @sec-training, the experience and labels documented in @sec-data, and the independent trials supporting its evaluated domain. While the initial archive bounds what the current evidence can support, new collection and re-qualification can widen that domain later. Part III relies on the current evaluation record rather than assuming that a policy manifest alone establishes competence. Its permission path checks the physical premises for each action and restricts or refuses proposals when those premises lack support. Any fallback still requires a response the machine can physically execute.
